- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast moderately, especially if recent price is falling.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >75% from prior day) are common; cap forecast at +10–15% above prior peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out extremes by averaging with 14-day moving average of history.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true trend reversal.
